Theme

piece noun

also chunk, bit

Traupman 72

1frustum: short u (Traupman frūstum, pp. 72, 360). A different word from frūstrā, “in vain”, whose u is long; Traupman himself prints frustum on pp. 282 and 336. Ruling: frūstrā with a long u.

frustum1, frustī n.

noun, second declension

piece or chunk

Other words

  • frustulum, frustulī n. — little piece

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

  • particula, particulae f. — a little bit, a small part of anything

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.162: tenuissimae particulae (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.28.23 (Lewis & Short)

    Not only of food: frustum is properly a piece of food, particula a little part of anything, as of sand in Horace (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Parvum frustum cape.

    Take a small piece.composed

  • pānis

    a piece of bread (often no separate word for “piece”)Traupman 360

See also crumb, slice, chop, cut.
